prompt: Input {"n": integer 0..30}. Return row n of Pascal's triangle: a list of n+1 integers, where row 0 is [1] and each inner entry is the sum of the two entries above it. The row starts and ends with 1, is symmetric, and sums to 2**n.
Input {"n": integer 0..10}. Return the n-bit reflected binary Gray code as a list of 2**n integers: element i equals i XOR (i >> 1). For n = 0 the list is [0].

Input {"nums": integer list}. Sort the values in increasing order and return the largest difference between two neighbouring values; return 0 if there are fewer than two values. The result is between 0 and max(nums) - min(nums).
Input {"n": integer 0..15}. Return how many strings made of exactly n "(" and n ")" characters are balanced (every prefix has at least as many "(" as ")"). n = 0 gives 1 (the empty string).
Input {"nums": integer list}. Return the value that occurs strictly more than len(nums)/2 times, or null if no value does (an empty list gives null).

Input {"nums": list of at least one integer, each -10..10}. Return a list of the same length whose element i is the product of all elements of nums except the one at index i (the product of no numbers is 1).

Input {"a": string, "b": string}. Return the length of the longest common subsequence of a and b (characters taken in order, not necessarily contiguous). The result is between 0 and min(len(a), len(b)); equal strings give their length.

Input {"s": string of decimal digits}. Count the ways to split s into consecutive pieces where every piece is a number from 1 to 26 written without leading zeros. The empty string gives 1; a string starting with "0" gives 0.
Input {"nums": integer list, "k": integer}. Return the number of index pairs (i, j) with i < j and nums[i] + nums[j] == k. The result is between 0 and len(nums)*(len(nums)-1)/2.
Input {"n": integer 0..10000}. Return a list of n+1 integers whose element i is the number of 1 bits in the binary form of i.

Input {"nums": list of integers, each 0..1000000000}. Return the sum, over all unordered pairs of positions, of the Hamming distance between the two values (the number of bit positions where they differ). Fewer than two values give 0.
Input {"nums": integer list}. Return, in increasing order, each distinct value that occurs more than once in nums (each such value once).
Input {"nums": integer list}. Return the distinct values of nums in the order of their first occurrence.
Input {"nums": integer list}. Return the length L of the longest sequence of consecutive integers x, x+1, ..., x+L-1 that all occur in nums (in any order, duplicates ignored). An empty list gives 0.

Input {"s": string, "t": string}. Return true if len(s) == len(t) and a one-to-one mapping of characters turns s into t (each character of s always maps to the same character of t, and no two characters of s map to the same one); otherwise false.

Input {"s": string, "rows": integer 1..1000}. Write the characters of s in a zigzag over the given number of rows (down from row 0 to the last row, then diagonally back up to row 0, and so on) and return the rows read left to right, top row first, concatenated. With one row, or at least as many rows as characters, the result is s.

Input {"matrix": nonempty square matrix of integers whose every row and every column is nondecreasing, "k": integer between 1 and the number of cells}. Return the k-th smallest value of the matrix, counting duplicates.

Input {"path": string that starts with "/"}. Return the canonical form of this absolute Unix path: "." segments are removed, ".." removes the previous segment (never going above the root), repeated slashes count as one, and there is no trailing slash except for the root "/" itself.

Input {"s": string}. Return the length of the longest subsequence of s (characters taken in order, not necessarily contiguous) that reads the same forwards and backwards. The empty string gives 0; a palindrome gives its own length.

Input {"gas": list of nonnegative integers, "cost": list of nonnegative integers of the same length}. Stations 0..n-1 lie on a circle. Starting with an empty tank at station s, at each station i you add gas[i] and then spend cost[i] to reach station (i+1) mod n; the tank must never go below zero. Return the smallest s from which you can visit all stations once and return to s, or -1 if there is none (also -1 for empty lists).
